Scaling Up Platform · Progress Update · July 6, 2026

Six releases in three days — every feature phase of the roadmap is now live

The July 3 update ended with "sliders and printing next up." Since then, six releases shipped to the live platform: the survey sliders and report printing, LVA peer benchmarks, the unlocked question editor, findings logic, a platform-hardening pass, and (as of this morning) conditional questions. That closes your items #4, #8, #9, #10, #11, #12 and #13 — and with them, every buildable phase of the roadmap. Everything below is shown, not described: real screens from the production platform and from each release's launch verification against the production database.

1 · The survey sliders & report printing LIVE JULY 3

Your #8 (sliders), #4 (full-width answers) and #9 (group-report printing) — shipped the evening the last update went out.

#8 — the slider respondents actually use. LIVE The track is visibly thicker and easier to grab, and tapping any number under the track jumps the slider straight to it — exactly the click-to-set behavior drawn in the July 2 mock. This is the live survey, on all three participant surfaces (invited, public, quick-assessment).
#9 — Print / Download PDF, on every group report. LIVE The button at the top of this production LVA group report produces a clean 6-page PDF (print layout QA'd page by page). While shipping this we also closed #4: free-form text answers now lay out full-width with the question above the answer — including a squeeze nobody had reported yet, where long text answers were being crushed into a 96-pixel rating column on LVA reports. Found during pre-release QA, fixed in the same release.

2 · Peer benchmarks for the LVA LIVE JULY 4

Your #12 (the ability to set peer averages) and #13 (peer comparison in both LVA reports).

#13 — peers inline in the group report. LIVE Each rating row gains a Peers value with a signed deviation — green ▲ where the team beats its peers, red ▼ where it trails. Factors without a peer value simply omit the comparison, so a partially-filled benchmark set never breaks a report.
#13 — and in the individual report. LIVE A "compared to peers" section in the individual LVA report, in the natural spot after the ratings. One honest note: these two verification shots used temporary numbers entered against the production database and cleared before launch — we never invent benchmark data. Which means the live reports are peer-free today, waiting on one thing: #12 gives you a "Peer averages" panel on the LVA template editor. Enter your real peer numbers there and both reports light up instantly — no release needed.

3 · The question editor, unlocked LIVE JULY 5

Your #10 — add and edit questions of every type, directly on the platform. The engine already supported all four question types; the editor only exposed sliders. That gap is closed.

Before — July 1
After — on production today

The type dropdown is enabled — SLIDER, TEXT, NUMBER and MULTI_CHOICE — and choosing multiple-choice opens an options editor with add/remove and a "max choices" cap that the live survey enforces. The after-shot is the editor on production this morning, on a real draft. Question identifiers are generated automatically and human-readable (S1_pick_your_top_two_obstacles), and once a question is published its identity is locked — so trend history and the Esperto import mapping can never silently break, no matter what gets edited later.

The end-to-end proof. A test instrument authored entirely in the editor — text, number and multiple-choice questions — taken as a survey and rendered on a report, with the chosen options shown as their labels. The launch check also caught and same-day-fixed two real defects: a pre-existing bug where a follow-up save could silently delete just-saved questions, and multiple-choice answers displaying as raw internal keys on reports. Both are the reason every release gets walked end-to-end before it counts as done.

4 · Findings logic — answer-driven recommendations LIVE JULY 6

Your #11 — report text that reacts to what the respondent answered, authorable per question, on every question type.

Where you author it — the Findings panel, live on the production editor. LIVE Every scoreable question gains a collapsible Findings panel: score bands with a message on sliders and number questions (with a coverage hint so gaps in the bands can't surprise you at publish), and per-option text on multiple-choice. Editable on existing questions too — that's the point: add findings to the live LVA and QSP instruments without rebuilding them.
Where it lands — both report families. Scored reports merge the fired findings into "What to work on next" (top); qualitative reports like the LVA and QSP gain a consolidated findings section (bottom) — the first time those instruments can carry answer-driven recommendations at all. Two guarantees worth knowing: findings are frozen into each submission at scoring time, so a report someone already received can never quietly change; and the SU-Full's 305 existing recommendation bands were regression-proven byte-identical. Ships empty by design — open any draft, write findings per question, publish, and new campaigns render them.

5 · The hardening pass — protecting what's live LIVE JULY 6

With every feature phase shipped, this release deliberately added no new features — it hardened the platform four ways while the import phase waits on your export files.

Broken scoring can no longer publish. LIVE The July 5 launch check surfaced a lurking gap: a template whose scoring tiers didn't fully cover the score range would publish fine — and then reject every single submission. Now publish itself blocks it, with a plain-English message naming the fix. A scan of all 19 published versions on production confirmed zero real templates were affected; the only offender was the disposable test template that uncovered the gap.
Imported history is now visibly labeled. LIVE Anything brought over from Esperto carries an "Imported from Esperto (historical)" badge everywhere it renders — respondent reports, group reports, and the campaign screen — so nobody ever mistakes migrated history for fresh platform data. This lands ahead of the Rockefeller/LVA history imports, so provenance is honest from day one. Two quieter items shipped alongside: import failures now email the admin inbox within ~10 minutes (previously, spotting one meant a human reading server logs), and report pages now tolerate slow database connections instead of intermittently erroring.

6 · Conditional questions — the greyed-out tab, made real LIVE TODAY

Since May the template editor has carried a disabled "Conditional Logic — v1.5" tab. As of this morning that promise is a shipped feature: any question can be shown only when a respondent picks a specific option on an earlier multiple-choice question.

Where you author it — "Show only when…", live on the production editor. LIVE Two dropdowns on any question: pick an earlier multiple-choice question, pick one of its options — done. The editor protects you from every wrong turn: required questions can't be made conditional (a hidden required question would trap the respondent), deleting a question that others depend on warns you by name, and a broken rule can't reach respondents because publishing is blocked with a plain-English message until it's fixed.
What respondents see. The launch-verification survey: a "biggest obstacle?" question where ticking People and Cash made their two "why?" follow-ups appear in place — untick one and its follow-up (and any half-typed answer) vanishes. It works across pages too: a follow-up section whose questions are all hidden disappears from the page count entirely ("Section 1 of 1" became "Section 1 of 2" the moment an option was ticked) — no more walking respondents through pages that don't apply to them.
What the report shows — only the picked path. The same submission's report: the People follow-ups are there, the Cash question is nowhere — the report reads like the respondent's actual conversation. This is the pattern the LVA has always had ("only explain the obstacles you picked"), now available on every instrument you author — including the two new assessments you've been building in the editor. It's tamper-proof too: a hand-crafted submission trying to smuggle in answers to hidden questions gets those answers stripped by the server before anything is stored.
The guardrail, caught in the act. During launch verification we deliberately dragged a conditional question above the question that controls it — and publish refused, naming the exact question and the fix. Broken conditional logic cannot reach a respondent. (Like findings, this ships empty: no live instrument changed today. Add a "Show only when…" rule to any draft, publish, and new campaigns honor it.)
